options.name: progression_balancing
options.description:
A system that can move progression earlier, to try and prevent the player from getting stuck and bored early.

A lower setting means more getting stuck. A higher setting means less getting stuck.

options.name: accessibility
options.description:
Set rules for reachability of your items/locations.

**Full:** ensure everything can be reached and acquired.

**Minimal:** ensure what is needed to reach your goal can be acquired.

options.name: initial_weapon
options.description: Which weapon will you have at the beginning of the run.

options.name: aspectsanity
options.description:
How you'll get the various weapon aspects.
unlocked: every Aspect is available from the start, fully upgraded.
randomized: all 24 Aspects are shuffled - the 18 alternates and each weapon's Aspect of
Melinoe, which weapons no longer come with for free. Each is its own item, granted at
max level. Your starting weapon begins on a random one of its 4 Aspects, but only at
level 1 - that Aspect's item is still out there and maxes it out when you find it.
Every other weapon starts with no Aspect at all. Aspect levels can't be bought at the
Cauldron; they only come from items.
progressive: you start with only Melinoe's Aspect. Each weapon gets "Progressive
<Weapon> Aspect" items - the first unlocks its other aspects, the rest upgrade them
(up to rank 5). Normal unlocking and upgrading is blocked.
per_aspect: all 24 Aspects level independently, each with its own "Progressive
<Aspect>" item - 5 copies apiece (1 unlock + 4 rank upgrades), 120 items total. Your
starting weapon begins with a random one of its 4 Aspects at rank 1. With Weapon/Aspect
Combine on, the first aspect item you receive for a weapon also unlocks that weapon;
with it off, each weapon unlock is its own item.

options.name: weapon_aspect_combine
options.description:
Setting removes "Unlock <Weapon>" checks. Instead you unlock a weapon the first time
you gain access to one of its aspects.

options.name: location_system
options.description:
How to handle base locations.
Room_based: Each location is the first time you clear that many rooms/encounters in one
run. For example; Room Check 9 sends the first time you clear 9 encounters in one run.
Point_based: Each location is a point total you must accumulate, you get points equal
to a room's depth when you clear it. Use this for much longer APs, and it will likely
be quite repetitive.
Per_Weapon_Room_Based: Like room_based, but there are separate pools for each weapon.

options.name: score_rewards_amount
options.description:
Point_based only. How many score locations are there? If you set each route to have
it's own pool later, each route will have a pool this big. If there aren't enough
locations to fulfill the minimum item pool, this will be increased accordingly. More
locations means more filler items, which are beneficial, but not required.

options.name: enemy_locations
options.description: Add locations for the first time you defeat each enemy type.

options.name: npc_locations
options.description: Add locations for the first time you speak to each NPC.

options.name: graspsanity
options.description:
Adds Progressive Grasp items to the pool; each one raises your maximum Grasp. You
start at 0. If you turn this off, I highly recommend adding psyche to the filler pool.

options.name: grasp_count
options.description: How many Progressive Grasp items in the item pool.

options.name: grasp_intervals
options.description: How much each Progressive Grasp raises your maximum Grasp.

options.name: arcanasanity
options.description:
How Arcana Cards are obtained.
false: unlocked normally by purchasing at the Altar of Ashes. Highly recommend
adjusting filler checks if you go with this.
arcana: each card is unlocked by an item and can't be purchased, but still upgrades
normally.
progressive_arcana: each card gets multiple progressive items - the first unlocks it,
the rest upgrade it. Cards can't be upgraded any other way.

options.name: keepsakesanity
options.description:
How Keepsakes are handled.
false: unchanged from the base game.
randomized: Adds a location for earning each keepsake, and adds each keepsake to the item pool.
progressive: Adds a location for earning each keepsake, and adds 3 "Progressive
Keepsake" items. The first unlocks all keepsakes at level one, the next two level
them up. Normal keepsake leveling is blocked.

options.name: petsanity
options.description:
How Familiars (pets: Frinos, Toula, Raki, Hecuba, Gale) are handled. Items only - no new check locations.
unlocked: every familiar is available from the start.
randomized: each familiar becomes its own item; you start with none and unlock each
at maximum bond when you receive its item.
progressive: a Progressive Familiar item is added - the first unlocks all familiars,
the rest upgrade their bonds. Normal familiar unlocking/bonding is blocked.

options.name: deathlink
options.description: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

options.name: deathlink_percent
options.description:
When you receive a DeathLink, how much of your health you'll lose, as a percentage of
your maximum health. Or, set to 0 to end the run regardless of available death defiances.

options.name: deathlink_amnesty
options.description:
How many times you die in a row before it sends a Deathlink to everyone else. 0
means you'll never send, only receive

options.name: no_death_on_winning_runs
options.description:
After winning a run, you don't send a deathlink for returning back to the crossroads.
I don't know why you would want to turn this off.

options.name: reverse_vow
options.description:
Start each run with the vows below already active (raising difficulty); each is then
removed, one at a time, by items found in the multiworld.

options.name: vow_pain
options.description: How many levels of Vow of Pain to start with (foes deal more damage).

options.name: vow_grit
options.description: How many levels of Vow of Grit to start with (foes have more health).

options.name: vow_wards
options.description: How many levels of Vow of Wards to start with (foes gain Barrier).

options.name: vow_frenzy
options.description: How many levels of Vow of Frenzy to start with (foes are faster).

options.name: vow_hordes
options.description: How many levels of Vow of Hordes to start with (more foes).

options.name: vow_menace
options.description: How many levels of Vow of Menace to start with (foes from the next region).

options.name: vow_return
options.description: How many levels of Vow of Return to start with (slain foes may revive).

options.name: vow_fangs
options.description: How many levels of Vow of Fangs to start with (armored foes gain perks).

options.name: vow_scars
options.description: How many levels of Vow of Scars to start with (healing is less effective).

options.name: vow_debt
options.description: How many levels of Vow of Debt to start with (Higher gold costs).

options.name: vow_shadow
options.description: How many levels of Vow of Shadow to start with (Shadow Servants).

options.name: vow_forfeit
options.description: How many levels of Vow of Forfeit to start with (first Boon becomes Red Onion).

options.name: vow_time
options.description: How many levels of Vow of Time to start with (time limit per region).

options.name: vow_void
options.description: How many levels of Vow of Void to start with (less Grasp for Arcana).

options.name: vow_hubris
options.description: How many levels of Vow of Hubris to start with (Primes Magick after Boons).

options.name: vow_denial
options.description: How many levels of Vow of Denial to start with (unpicked blessings vanish).

options.name: vow_rivals
options.description: How many levels of Vow of Rivals to start with (Guardians are stronger).

options.name: reverse_rivals
options.description:
Reverse which Guardians the Vow of Rivals strengthens: this makes Chronos and Typhon
the last boss to return to normal.

options.name: goal_requires_chronos
options.description: Whether defeating Chronos (Underworld's final boss) is part of your Goal.

options.name: goal_requires_typhon
options.description: Whether defeating Typhon (Surface's final boss) is part of your Goal.

options.name: goal_requires_hades
options.description:
Whether defeating Hades (Nightmare route's final boss) is part of your goal. Requires
the "Zagreus_Journey" mod by NikkelM, which in turn requires Hades 1 be installed.

options.name: goal_requires_zagreus
options.description: Whether defeating Zagreus is part of your Goal.

options.name: goal_mode
options.description:
How the toggled-on Goal bosses above combine.
all_selected: every toggled-on boss must be defeated.
any_selected: defeating any one of the toggled-on bosses is enough.

options.name: zagreus_encounter_mode
options.description:
How Zagreus fights appear (only matters if Zagreus is part of your Goal):
Vanilla: Zagreus fights appear how they normally do in the late game.
Empowered: Zagreus fights appear how they normally do, but Zagreus starts heavily
empowered. Progressive Zagreus Weaken items are added to the multiworld that weaken him
back down to, and eventually below, his normal strength.
Final Challenge: Defeating any route's final boss spawns a contract to go fight Zagreus
instead of ending the run.

options.name: include_underworld
options.description: Whether to include the Hades 2 Underworld route (Erebus/Oceanus/Fields of Mourning/Tartarus).

options.name: include_surface
options.description: Whether to include the Surface route (City of Ephyra/Rift of Thessaly/Mount Olympus/The Summit).

options.name: include_nightmare
separate_checks
options.description:
When you've included more than one route: does each route get its own full set of
checks, or do they share one pool?
separate_pools: Every route gets their own locations, meaning you'll have to
thoroughly explore each of your routes.
combine_pools: the routes share one pool. Score checks stop being route-specific:
there are 200 of them total, every route's rooms bank into the same points pool, and
you could earn all 200 without ever leaving one route. Each room check is likewise
earned the first time you clear that depth on ANY route.

options.name: lock_routes
options.description:
Lock each route's regions behind its progressive route items (Progressive Underworld
/ Progressive Surface / Progressive Nightmare).

options.name: starting_route
options.description:
Which route is open from the start. The others open as you receive their progressive
route items (or, for Surface/Nightmare, their Access item).
Picking a route you didn't include snaps to one you did. A route your goal forces in
(e.g. the Surface when your goal requires Typhon) is still reachable, but it won't be
your starting route unless you chose it here.
all: every included route starts open, no unlock items needed.

options.name: start_with_surface_cure
options.description:
Start with the "Unraveling a Fateful Bond" incantation to remove Melinoe's curse in
the overworld. If this is turned off, it will be added to the item pool.

options.name: chronos_defeats_needed
options.description: How many times you must defeat Chronos to satisfy the Chronos part of the goal

options.name: typhon_defeats_needed
options.description: How many times you must defeat Typhon to satisfy the Typhon part of the goal

options.name: hades_defeats_needed
options.description: How many times you must defeat Hades to satisfy the Hades part of the goal.

options.name: zagreus_defeats_needed
options.description: How many times you must defeat Zagreus to satisfy the Zagreus part of the goal.

options.name: zagreus_weaken_tiers
options.description:
If Zagreus Encounter Mode is set to Empowered, how many "Progressive Zagreus Weaken"
items exist to weaken him.

options.name: weapons_clears_needed
options.description:
How many different weapons you must use to defeat any boss. Meaning defeating Chronos
with the axe and Typhon with the blades would count as 2 weapons.

options.name: arachne_armor
options.description:
Adds a "Starting Arachne Armor" item to the item pool, which grants you a random
Arachne silk armor at the start of each run. It's still lost when your armor breaks.

options.name: daedalus_upgrade
options.description:
Adds this many Daedalus Upgrade items to the pool. Each one grants a random Daedalus
Hammer upgrade for your equipped weapon at the start of each run.

options.name: nectar_pack_value
options.description: Amount of Nectar granted per Nectar item.

options.name: nectar_pack_percentage
options.description: Share of the filler pool that is Nectar.

options.name: starting_health_value
options.description: How much max health each Starting Max Health item grants.

options.name: starting_health_percentage
options.description: Share of the filler pool that is Max Health.

options.name: starting_magick_value
options.description: How much max Magick each Starting Max Magick item grants.

options.name: starting_magick_percentage
options.description: Share of the filler pool that is Max Magick.

options.name: starting_gold_value
options.description: How much run-start gold each Starting Gold item grants.

options.name: starting_gold_percentage
options.description: Share of the filler pool that is Starting Gold.

options.name: starting_armor_value
options.description: How much run-start armor each Starting Armor item grants.

options.name: starting_armor_percentage
options.description: Share of the filler pool that is Starting Armor.

options.name: rarity_increase_percentage
options.description:
Share of the filler pool that is Rarity Increase. Each one permanently raises your
odds of higher-rarity boons.

options.name: major_finds_percentage
options.description:
Share of the filler pool that is Increased Odds of Major Finds. Each one nudges door
rewards toward Major Finds (Boons, Daedalus Hammers, Centaur Hearts) and away from
Minor Finds (Bones, Ash, Nectar).

options.name: ashes_pack_value
options.description: Amount of Ashes granted per Ashes item.

options.name: ashes_pack_percentage
options.description: Share of the filler pool that is Ashes. I don't recommend this if Arcanasanity is on.

options.name: psyche_pack_value
options.description: Amount of Psyche granted per Psyche item.

options.name: psyche_pack_percentage
options.description: Share of the filler pool that is Psyche. I don't recommend this if Graspsanity is on.

options.name: moon_dust_pack_value
options.description: Amount of Moon dust granted per Moon dust item.

options.name: moon_dust_pack_percentage
options.description: Share of the filler pool that is Moon Dust. I don't recommend this if Arcanasanity is progressive_arcana.

options: Allow Orpheus to Spawn in Tartarus

options.name: exclude_locations
options.description: Prevent these locations from having an important item.

options.name: priority_locations

options.name: item_links
options.description: Share part of your item pool with other players.

options.name: plando_items
options.description: Generic items plando.

options.description:
Start with the specified amount of these items and don't place them in the world. Example: "Bomb: 1"

The game decides what the replacement items will be.
